preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (deployer)
At least one user must hold some NMETA tokens

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call setMaxTxAmount(0) to set the maximum transaction amount to zero. This will cause all transfer transactions to fail due to the require(amount <= maxTxAmount) check in _transfer(), effectively locking all user funds. No financial gain occurs, but contract functionality is disrupted.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The NowMeta contract has a setMaxTxAmount function that is only callable by the owner. Setting maxTxAmount to 0 will cause all transfers to fail because the _transfer function has require(amount <= maxTxAmount). This is an owner privilege abuse vulnerability where the owner can arbitrarily freeze all token transfers.
attempts.attack_strategy: Impersonate the contract owner and call setMaxTxAmount(0) to set the maximum transaction amount to zero, effectively locking all transfers.
attempts.step_by_step_plan:
1. Fork mainnet at a recent block
2. Create an interface for the NowMeta contract
3. Impersonate the contract owner using vm.prank()
4. Call setMaxTxAmount(0)
5. Verify that maxTxAmount is now 0
